diagnostic_evidence.quote: The power density in~\eqref{eqn:anp} is a monotonic function of the radius $r$. This implies that it is not possible to correctly reconstruct the circular crown.

issues.failure_explanation: The monotonicity estimate controls only the integral of the reference power density over D. It neither says that the density is pointwise small precisely on D nor excludes equally small values outside D. The paper's own connected hollow anomaly is a counterexample: its radial power density has disk-shaped sublevel sets, so the annular anomaly cannot be reconstructed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either prove a geometric characterization of a restricted class for which the power-density sublevel set equals D, or withdraw the general reconstruction claim and present the procedure only as a heuristic.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm has no general shape-reconstruction guarantee for the stated class of one or more connected anomalies; its output can instead fill cavities or convexify the target.

issues.failure_explanation: The upper estimate for P-P_b involves the pointwise factor (sigma_bg-sigma_a)/sigma_a relative to the power density sigma_bg|grad u_bg|^2. A lower bound on the resulting integral requires the reciprocal of the maximum of that ratio. The coefficient sigma_a^m/Delta_sigma is the reciprocal of a lower-extrema combination and need not control the maximum when the conductivities vary.
